```{python}
#| label: setup
import json
import sys

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")  # code runs from the project folder (execute-dir: project)
import analysis  # constants only; the numbers come from outputs/

clusters = pd.read_parquet("outputs/clusters.parquet")
prof = pd.read_csv("outputs/cluster_profiles.csv", index_col="cluster")
rho = pd.read_csv("outputs/irca_infant.csv")
s = json.loads(open("outputs/summary.json").read())
k = s["k"]
# The title states the number of clusters: fail loudly if the analysis changes it.
assert k == 4, f"k is now {k}: rename this post and its folder"
names = prof["name"].to_dict()
colors = prof["color"].to_dict()
rural = prof["urban_row_share"].idxmin()
```

Colombia's drinking water is not one story. Between 2016 and 2023 we followed the urban
head towns and rural areas of `{python} f"{s['municipalities']:,}"` municipalities, a total
of `{python} f"{s['kept']:,}"` zone-years with a utility-supplied ("prestadores")
water-quality score (IRCA, from INS open data). We let k-means sort them by nine features:
water quality, piped water and sewer coverage, poverty, rurality, altitude (derived from one
SRTM elevation point at the head town), rainfall, municipal performance and water transfers
per person.

It found `{python} k` kinds:

```{python}
#| output: asis
for c in prof.index:
    p = prof.loc[c]
    print(f"- **{c} · {names[c]}**: {p['rows']:,} zone-years from {p['municipalities']} "
          f"municipalities; median IRCA {p['irca_median']:.1f}, "
          f"{p['mean_water_coverage']:.0f}% piped water, {p['mean_ipm']:.0f}% poor.")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-pca
#| fig-cap: "Each dot is a zone-year, placed by the first two principal components of the nine features and coloured by kind. The kinds overlap: they summarise a continuum."
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of about eleven thousand dots in four coloured groups that overlap at their edges. The rural, unserved, high-risk group spreads to one side; the three town and city groups sit closer together."
plt.rcParams.update({"axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False})
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.4))
# Draw the outer kinds first, so the central one is not hidden under the others.
centres = clusters.groupby("cluster")[["pc1", "pc2"]].mean()
for c in (centres ** 2).sum(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False).index:
    g = clusters[clusters["cluster"] == c]
    ax.scatter(g["pc1"], g["pc2"], s=4, alpha=0.4, color=colors[c],
               marker=analysis.CLUSTER_MARKERS[c - 1], label=f"{c} · {names[c]}",
               rasterized=True)
ax.set_xlabel("PC1")
ax.set_ylabel("PC2")
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
by_id = sorted(zip(labels, handles))  # legend in kind order, whatever the drawing order
leg = ax.legend([h for _, h in by_id], [lab for lab, _ in by_id], markerscale=3,
                frameon=False, fontsize=8)
for handle in leg.legend_handles:
    handle.set_alpha(1)
plt.show()
```

The *`{python} names[rural]`* kind stands out: median IRCA
`{python} f"{prof.loc[rural, 'irca_median']:.1f}"`, in the high-risk band of Resolución 2115
de 2007, with `{python} f"{prof.loc[rural, 'mean_sewer_coverage']:.0f}"`% sewer coverage on
average.

## Does bad water go with worse outcomes?

Not in any simple way. The infant mortality series changes method in 2017, and 2020 looks
like a different source, so we compare 2017–2019 and 2021–2023 only. Within each kind, the
Spearman correlation between IRCA and infant mortality in those years is between
`{python} f"{rho['spearman_rho'].min():+.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{rho['spearman_rho'].max():+.2f}"`. That does **not** mean water quality does not
matter, and nothing here shows that it causes any outcome. Infant mortality is measured for
the whole municipality while IRCA describes one zone; poverty, rurality, health services and
reporting quality all get in the way; and many rural systems are never sampled.

The full method, tables and caveats are in the [report](../../report.qmd), the
[cluster page](../../clusters.qmd) and the [dashboard](../../dashboard.qmd).
